key_insight: Ligand-engineered AgBiS2 nanocrystal films enable thicker near-infrared absorbers and 24.0%-efficient four-terminal tandems with lead-halide perovskite cells.
engineering_relevance: Improved charge extraction in thicker AgBiS2 films offers a route toward stable, scalable near-infrared sub-cells for thin-film tandem photovoltaics.
method: Model tandem performance using measured AgBiS2 absorption spectra.
Use solution-phase ligand exchange for one-step deposition of passivated nanocrystals.
Integrate AgBiS2 with visible-absorbing perovskite cells in four-terminal and monolithic tandems.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 24.0% four-terminal tandem efficiency, voltage addition in monolithic tandems, and >90% efficiency retention for AgBiS2 cells after three months in dry air without encapsulation.
watch_item: The >47.9% triple-junction efficiency is a modeled projection, while storage stability does not establish long-term operational durability.
paper_title: Stable AgBiS2 near-infrared absorbers for thin film tandem photovoltaics
